summary: A single-camera VLM combines images, ego history, navigation, and text instructions to produce driving trajectories and optional explanations. The ZERON team's technical report documents its runner-up solution in the CVPR 2024 end-to-end driving challenge.

name: OmniReason
title: OmniReason: A Temporal-Guided Vision-Language-Action Framework for Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official implementation was located in the checked primary paper and targeted public search.
summary: Introduces temporally grounded driving annotations and a VLA agent with sparse temporal memory. Spatiotemporal knowledge distillation links dynamic scene context to driving decisions and human-readable explanations.

name: DriveQA
title: DriveQA: Passing the Driving Knowledge Test
codeNote: Official repository includes CARLA question-answer data-generation Python scripts, verified by opening generate_T_intersection_QA_CARLA.py. This verifies dataset-generation code, not every model-training experiment.
summary: Evaluates language and multimodal models on driving rules, signage, and right-of-way reasoning. Text questions and controlled synthetic scenes expose gaps in numerical and spatial reasoning; training on the benchmark can improve downstream driving question answering.

name: STRIDE-QA
title: STRIDE-QA: Visual Question Answering Dataset for Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Urban Driving Scenes
codeNote: Verified benchmark.py plus inference runners, metric/parser utilities and visualization code. This is a benchmark/evaluation toolkit; full training reproduction was not verified.
summary: Builds driving question-answer pairs from multi-sensor recordings in Tokyo with dense spatial and temporal annotations. The benchmark measures object and ego-centric localization and future-motion reasoning, revealing limitations of general-purpose VLMs.

name: FastDriveVLA
title: FastDriveVLA: Efficient End-to-End Driving via Plug-and-Play Reconstruction-based Token Pruning
summary: FastDriveVLA reduces visual-token cost with a plug-and-play reconstruction-based pruning method that preserves task-relevant image regions for efficient end-to-end driving.

name: ReAL-AD
title: ReAL-AD: Towards Human-Like Reasoning in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
codeNote: The official project page has an inactive GitHub label; no author implementation was located.
summary: Augments end-to-end driving with strategic, tactical, and operational reasoning. VLM-derived context informs driving intent and maneuver choices, while a hierarchical decoder translates these decisions into trajectories.

name: BetterCheck
title: BetterCheck: Towards Safeguarding VLMs for Automotive Perception Systems
codeNote: No official implementation was located in the checked primary paper and targeted public search.
summary: Studies hallucinations in traffic-scene descriptions from proprietary and open VLMs. Repeated caption generation and self-consistency checks assess unsupported object statements, exposing tradeoffs between rejecting hallucinations and retaining valid detections.

name: AutoVLA
title: AutoVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Adaptive Reasoning and Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
summary: AutoVLA unifies language reasoning and feasible trajectory tokens in one model, with fast and chain-of-thought modes and reinforcement fine-tuning to reduce needless reasoning.

name: ReCogDrive
title: ReCogDrive: A Reinforced Cognitive Framework for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: ReCogDrive couples hierarchical driving-cognition data and a VLM with a diffusion planner, then applies reinforcement learning to improve trajectory safety and comfort.

name: V2X-UniPool
title: V2X-UniPool: Unifying Multimodal Perception and Knowledge Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
codeNote: The author-linked repository contains only a scene-prompt string in scene_prompt.py, example infrastructure data, and notes. This is a prompt/data resource, not a verified executable implementation of the knowledge-pool/RAG/planning system.
summary: Converts cooperative sensor observations into a time-indexed language knowledge pool. Retrieval of static and dynamic context grounds VLM reasoning and motion planning in current traffic information while reducing the amount of data communicated between agents.

name: DiffVLA
title: DiffVLA: Vision-Language Guided Diffusion Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: DiffVLA combines VLM-guided decisions with a sparse-dense diffusion policy, using agent and map interactions to guide multimodal trajectory generation.

name: DriveMoE
title: DriveMoE: Mixture-of-Experts for Vision-Language-Action Model in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveMoE routes camera views and driving behaviors to specialized vision and action experts, aiming to handle varied maneuvers without averaging distinct actions.

name: LightEMMA
title: LightEMMA: A Longitudinal Evaluation of Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
summary: LightEMMA evaluates successive VLMs under one lightweight, untuned driving protocol and finds that newer or larger models do not reliably improve prediction performance.

name: OpenDriveVLA
title: OpenDriveVLA: Towards End-to-end Autonomous Driving with Large Vision Language Action Model
summary: OpenDriveVLA aligns structured 2D/3D visual tokens with language and models agent-ego interactions to generate grounded trajectories and answer driving questions.
codeNote: Model and inference code are public; training scripts remain pending.

name: Cosmos-Reason1
title: Cosmos-Reason1: From Physical Common Sense To Embodied Reasoning
summary: Cosmos-Reason1 trains multimodal models for physical common sense and embodied decision-making, using structured reasoning data, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

name: SimLingo
title: SimLingo: Vision-Only Closed-Loop Autonomous Driving with Language-Action Alignment
summary: SimLingo aligns camera-based driving, visual question answering, and language-conditioned actions in one VLM policy. Its Action Dreaming supervision connects verbal instructions to possible future trajectories, helping language understanding remain consistent with closed-loop behavior.

name: AlphaDrive
title: AlphaDrive: Unleashing the Power of VLMs in Autonomous Driving via Reinforcement Learning and Reasoning
summary: AlphaDrive applies planning-specific reinforcement-learning rewards and a two-stage reasoning-and-planning training strategy to improve VLM driving decisions.

name: EMMA
title: EMMA: End-to-End Multimodal Model for Autonomous Driving
summary: EMMA maps camera inputs to trajectories, objects, and road graphs in a unified multimodal language space, with joint training improving performance across these tasks.

name: DriVLMe
title: DriVLMe: Enhancing LLM-Based Autonomous Driving Agents with Embodied and Social Experiences
summary: DriVLMe explores conversational, long-horizon driving with a video-language agent grounded in simulator experience and human dialogue, and documents its remaining real-world interaction and latency challenges.

name: DriveVLM
title: DriveVLM: The Convergence of Autonomous Driving and Large Vision-Language Models
summary: DriveVLM uses staged scene description, analysis, and hierarchical planning for complex scenarios; DriveVLM-Dual pairs it with a conventional driving stack and is tested on a production vehicle.
codeNote: The official GitHub repository hosts the paper and project website; model implementation is not released.

name: VLP
title: VLP: Vision Language Planning for Autonomous Driving
summary: VLP combines vision and language context for driving planning, targeting reasoning and long-tail generalization in urban scenes.

name: DriveLM
title: DriveLM: Driving with Graph Visual Question Answering
summary: DriveLM formulates driving perception, prediction, and planning as graph-structured visual question answering and releases data and an agent baseline.

name: DriveMLM
title: DriveMLM: Aligning Multi-Modal Large Language Models with Behavioral Planning States for Autonomous Driving
summary: DriveMLM connects multimodal language decisions to standard behavioral-planning states, enabling an LLM to make explainable closed-loop decisions within existing driving stacks.
codeNote: The official README lists code, models, dataset, and annotations as unreleased.

name: LMDrive
title: LMDrive: Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving with Large Language Models
summary: LMDrive follows natural-language instructions in closed-loop driving by combining language with multimodal sensors, and introduces instruction-following data and the LangAuto benchmark.

name: Dolphins
title: Dolphins: Multimodal Language Model for Driving
summary: Dolphins instruction-tunes a multimodal language model for driving tasks, using grounded chain-of-thought to support scene understanding, instruction following, in-context adaptation, and reflection.
codeNote: Inference code and checkpoint are public; training code and benchmark release remain pending.

name: On the Road with GPT-4V
title: On the Road with GPT-4V(ision): Early Explorations of Visual-Language Model on Autonomous Driving
summary: On the Road with GPT-4V evaluates a multimodal model on driving-scene understanding, causal reasoning, and decisions, highlighting both its promise and gaps in spatial grounding and traffic-signal perception.
codeNote: Official test images, prompts, and responses are public; this repository is an exploration archive rather than a released driving implementation.

name: LanguageMPC
title: LanguageMPC: Large Language Models as Decision Makers for Autonomous Driving
summary: LanguageMPC uses LLM reasoning for complex driving decisions and translates them into commands for low-level controllers, targeting interpretability and generalization.

name: LLM-Driver
title: Driving with LLMs: Fusing Object-Level Vector Modality for Explainable Autonomous Driving
summary: Driving with LLMs aligns object-level vector inputs with a language model and introduces a 160K-pair driving QA dataset for explainable decisions and action generation.

name: GPT-Driver
title: GPT-Driver: Learning to Drive with GPT
summary: GPT-Driver casts motion planning as language generation, prompting and fine-tuning GPT to output coordinate-based trajectories with natural-language reasoning.

name: DriveGPT4
title: DriveGPT4: Interpretable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Large Language Model
summary: DriveGPT4 fine-tunes a multimodal LLM on driving video and instruction data to explain vehicle behavior, answer questions, and predict low-level controls.

name: DiLu
title: DiLu: A Knowledge-Driven Approach to Autonomous Driving with Large Language Models
summary: DiLu equips an LLM driving agent with reasoning, reflection, and memory so it can accumulate experience and generalize decisions beyond fixed driving data.

name: Drive as You Speak
title: Drive as You Speak: Enabling Human-Like Interaction with Large Language Models in Autonomous Vehicles
summary: Drive as You Speak outlines an LLM-based vehicle framework that combines natural-language interaction, contextual reasoning, and specialized tools with existing driving modules.

name: DOROTHIE
title: DOROTHIE: Spoken Dialogue for Handling Unexpected Situations in Interactive Autonomous Driving Agents
summary: DOROTHIE introduces an interactive simulator and spoken-dialogue navigation benchmark for studying how driving agents handle unexpected events through human communication.

name: ActWorld-JEPA
title: ActWorld-JEPA: Action-Conditioned JEPA World Models Meet Latent Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
codeNote: Inference code, configurations, model artifacts and benchmark guides are public; the repository explicitly excludes a complete from-scratch training recipe.
summary: Conditions recurrent latent prediction on candidate trajectories and reranks plans using agreement and discrepancy between plan and future representations.

name: NWM
title: Breaking survivorship bias in driving world models
codeNote: Public release contains inference.py, model code, configurations, example input and trained weights; no training pipeline was verified.
summary: Learns routine and dangerous futures jointly from driving and accident videos, then evaluates imagined outcomes to select candidate driving actions.

name: NegWAM
title: Reinforcing End-to-End Autonomous Driving Safety via Negative-Aware Planning in a Unified World-Action Model
codeNote: Repository contains NAVSIM code, data caching and inference/evaluation scripts; released weights are linked on the author's Hugging Face. Complete training and HUGSIM release was not verified.
summary: Uses near-expert unsafe trajectories as repulsive anchors during flow-matching post-training and learns scene–trajectory compatibility with auxiliary rider tokens.

name: WAM-Sim0.1
title: WAM-Sim0.1: World Anchored Memory Meets Online RL for Consistent and Realistic Driving Simulation
codeNote: Official project page has Code and Hugging Face labels but no actionable resource links; omit the GitHub icon.
summary: Anchors driving video rollouts with persistent road, scene and instance memory, then refines generated rollouts with online flow-matching reinforcement learning.

name: GuidedWAM
title: GuidedWAM: Training-Free Energy Guidance for World Action Models in Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official code or project link verified from arXiv and title-specific searches.
summary: Adds differentiable driving objectives to frozen world-action models during sampling using scheduled, normalized and velocity-bounded energy guidance.

name: INTERACT
title: INTERACT: Learning Interaction-Aware World Dynamics from Driving Videos for Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official code or project link verified from arXiv and title-specific searches.
summary: Learns recurrent object slots, latent ego actions and action-conditioned future slots from unlabeled driving videos, then distills them into a trajectory planner.

name: Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0
title: Xiaomi Auto World Model 2.0: Causal World Models for Real-World Driving and Embodied Intelligence
codeNote: Official project page and technical report are public; no implementation repository linked on the project page.
summary: Combines view-temporal attention, persistent reconstructed 3D scene context and efficient streaming attention for multi-view generation and simulation.

name: GATS
title: Let LiDAR Decide Where to Look: Geometry-Measured Token Selection for Efficient Sparse Latent World Models
summary: GATS projects LiDAR and radar measurements into the camera view to select patches before visual encoding. A latent world model predicts the future features and motion of the retained tokens. The paper compares planning accuracy and compute at different token budgets on nuScenes and NAVSIM.

name: DriveUniTok
title: DriveUniTok: A Unified Multimodal Tokenizer for Driving World-Action Models
summary: DriveUniTok compresses camera appearance, projected LiDAR depth and ego motion into one decodable latent. A diffusion world-action model, DriveUniWAM, predicts future unified latents that decode into scene observations and ego trajectories. NAVSIM experiments evaluate prediction and planning, with an additional reinforcement-learning post-training stage.

name: Dream2Assist
title: Dream to Assist: Intent-Conditioned World Models for Shared Vehicle Control
codeNote: The earlier Dream2Assist repository was not verified as implementing this 2026 extension.
summary: Dream2Assist augments a recurrent state-space world model with driver-intent inference and trains an assistive policy through fictitious co-play. This extension adds human-data augmentation, reward restructuring and a deployment workflow, evaluated in racing and urban human studies plus preliminary vehicle trials. It studies shared control rather than fully autonomous driving.

name: CADRE
title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
summary: CADRE studies how video compression affects interactive world models using a family of causal autoencoders with frozen visual features and a distilled diffusion decoder. Identical action-conditioned world models are trained across compression settings, including driving on PhysicalAI-AV. The study compares rollout quality, action following and latency; it is a cross-domain representation study with explicit driving experiments.

name: OccWAM
title: OccWAM: Occupancy World-Action Models with Joint Scene-to-Ego Flow Matching
summary: OccWAM jointly generates future occupancy and ego trajectories. A scene-centric prediction is re-indexed into predicted ego frames for a second joint refinement stage. Experiments cover closed-loop driving, open-loop planning, and occupancy forecasting, with different input protocols across tasks.

name: MORE
title: MORE: Learning Motion-Oriented Registers for Driving World Models and Planning
summary: MORE learns compact motion-conditioned registers during video pretraining using masked patch prediction and register masking. The same register space then supports future-state prediction, trajectory generation, and scoring, aligning the pretrained representation with downstream world modeling and planning.

name: SimVTA
title: SimVTA: Simulation-Grounded Video-Trajectory Alignment for Driving World Action Models
summary: SimVTA renders future videos for alternative high-reward trajectories in reconstructed scenes, then combines trajectory GRPO with matched-video flow supervision. Prioritizing difficult rendered futures improves shared representations. The model predicts trajectories without simulator calls at inference.
codeNote: Official repository currently contains results and documentation; implementation and checkpoints remain on its release checklist.

name: PlanWAM
title: PlanWAM: Planning-Shaped Future Representations for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
codeNote: Code and models announced; repository currently contains only README and LICENSE.
summary: Shapes a privileged future latent with trajectory-planning objectives, then distills it into a history-only predictor. A temporal register pyramid compresses observations, while the predicted future guides trajectory generation and selection. Evaluates planning on NAVSIM v1/v2 and zero-shot closed-loop transfer on HUGSIM.

name: GeoWM
title: GeoWM: Efficient Direct World Modeling in Explicit Geometry
summary: Forecasts scene geometry directly at a requested future horizon from RGB-derived geometric history. A camera-motion predictor supplies a projected geometry prior to a flow-matching transformer, avoiding recursive rollouts. Evaluated on driving, aerial-flight and manipulation datasets; it is a forecasting model rather than a complete driving policy.

name: TerrainForge
title: TerrainForge: Physics-Grounded road geometry Editing for Counterfactual Autonomous Driving
summary: TerrainForge edits road geometry and friction in reconstructed driving scenes while recomputing vehicle dynamics, camera viewpoints, and clearance. A learned surrogate screens proposed edits by their predicted safety effects before expensive multi-vehicle counterfactual rollouts.

name: ReWAM
title: ReWAM: Reciprocal World Action Models for Interactive Autonomous Driving
codeNote: Inference only; training is excluded. Evaluation requires oracle agent states.
summary: Models ego and surrounding agents as reciprocal conditional responders within a shared future-world representation. Role-specific action transformers exchange strategy tokens through a Level-k hierarchy and learn demonstration-conditioned responses via flow matching. Evaluated on NAVSIM, with emphasis on interactive traffic scenarios.

name: PhysWAM
title: PhysWAM: Physically Consistent World Action Model for Autonomous Driving
codeNote: Code release announced in the paper; no implementation repository verified.
summary: Jointly generates multi-view video, metric depth and ego motion in one flow-matching transformer. Coupled Point Projection connects generated depth and motion through LiDAR-grounded geometric supervision. Uses a label-free trajectory consensus rule and evaluates planning, depth/video prediction and zero-shot closed-loop transfer.

name: V2X-WAM
title: V2X-WAM: A Cooperative World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Fuses vehicle and infrastructure observations into a reliability-aware representation with compact communication. Proposed trajectories condition future occupancy and dynamic-flow prediction, whose outputs refine the final plan. Evaluated on the V2X-Seq-SPD validation split for cooperative planning and future-world prediction.

name: AD-E2E-JEPA
title: AD-E2E-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture For End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: AD-E2E-JEPA introduces a regularized projector that compresses visual patch embeddings for efficient action-conditioned world-model rollouts. It evaluates goal-conditioned planning without a trained driving policy, using ground-truth future observations as goals, and also studies downstream imitation learning.
codeNote: Main source code released; training and evaluation launchers target Slurm and require local adaptation.

name: DreamStream
title: DreamStream: Towards Policy-Oriented Generative Simulation for End-to-End Driving
summary: DreamStream is a policy-oriented generative simulator that preserves decision-relevant scene structure for closed-loop driving evaluation and introduces the interactive Navhard-CL benchmark.

name: ForeDrive
title: ForeDrive: Foresight-Guided End-to-End Autonomous Driving with a Planning-Relevant Latent World Model
summary: ForeDrive conditions a diffusion planner on multi-horizon futures predicted by a JEPA-style latent world model. Gated fusion, future-status cues, and trajectory-adaptive bias connect imagined futures to planning while retaining reliable current observations, using imitation learning without a separate scorer.

name: DriveReferee
title: DriveReferee: Geometric Safety Verdicts Need Not Be Learned for Driving World-Action Models
codeNote: Implementation released; checkpoints pending.
summary: Predicts scene geometry and applies explicit collision and drivable-area checks to world-action-model trajectories. During training, geometric verdicts form preferences for policy distillation; at deployment, the same rules select among candidates using predicted state. Evaluated on NAVSIM with a single front camera.

name: ZYT-World
title: ZYT-World: A Real-Time Controllable World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous-Driving Simulation
summary: ZYT-World targets low-latency, controllable seven-camera driving simulation, combining camera-specific conditioning, one-step streaming generation, and place memory.

name: MM-Future
title: MM-Future: Multi-Mode Joint World-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: MM-Future jointly generates multiple paired future-scene and ego-action hypotheses, then scores candidate trajectories using their predicted futures.

name: SV-WAM
title: SV-WAM: An Efficient Surround-View World-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: SV-WAM uses six-camera future-video prediction as training supervision for a shared world-action model, then removes the video branch for efficient planning.

name: VATIX
title: How Far Can 5,500 Hours of Driving Take You? A Scaling Law Analysis of Video Diffusion Models
summary: This study analyzes video-diffusion scaling on up to 5,500 hours of driving data and finds training exposure especially effective under fixed compute, while larger models improve asymptotic quality.

name: BehaviorWorldGen
title: BehaviorWorldGen: Closing the Loop between Action Models and World Simulators via Controllable Behavior-Aware Structured World Generation
summary: BehaviorWorldGen generates controllable multi-agent traffic rollouts whose agents respond to the ego and one another, then uses rendered scenarios to refine driving policies.

name: WA-JEPA
title: WA-JEPA: Rethinking the Video JEPA Paradigm for World-Action Modeling in Autonomous Driving
summary: WA-JEPA adapts video JEPA to action-conditioned driving futures with future-masked training, latent flow matching, and joint future-scene/trajectory prediction.

name: RISE
title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
summary: RISE adaptively decides whether to continue world-model rollouts based on expected planning benefit and compute cost, supported by counterfactual risk data.

name: DA-WAM
title: DA-WAM: Decision-Aligned Future Latents for Driving World Models
summary: DA-WAM jointly trains action-conditioned future latents and trajectory scoring so each candidate is evaluated against its own predicted consequences.

name: 4D-WAM
title: 4D-WAM: 4D Consistent World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: 4D-WAM uses geometric-model supervision to improve the physical consistency of predicted driving futures and emphasizes early denoising stages where planning decisions form.

name: SimWAM
title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: SimWAM uses future video as training-only supervision for a lightweight action expert, avoiding video generation at inference and adding reinforcement learning for driving rewards.

name: SUV
title: SUV: Future Scene Understanding as Video Generation for End-to-End Driving
summary: SUV predicts future visual, semantic, depth, and agent-dynamics streams with a shared video model, then conditions an action expert on those futures for trajectory planning.
codeNote: Checkpoint and inference code are public; training and the WOD-E2E pipeline remain pending.

name: Auto-JEPA
title: Auto-JEPA: A Latent World Model of Continuous Intent for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Auto-JEPA predicts a continuous future-driving-intent embedding and retrieves/ranks executable trajectories, avoiding dense future-scene reconstruction and a learned trajectory generator.

name: INTACT
title: INTACT: Isomorphic Intent-to-Action Learning for Search-Free World Models
summary: INTACT learns an intent-to-action interface from reward-free trajectories, enabling a direct policy from latent goals while retaining optional sampling or local search.

name: HyWorldVLA
title: HyWorldVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Hybrid World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: HyWorldVLA combines pixel-level video reconstruction with latent future prediction during training, then uses future latents to guide trajectory generation.

name: GeoWorldAD

summary: GeoWorldAD grounds planning in present 3D geometry and predicted future geometry, iteratively refining trajectories to balance safety and progress.

name: OWMDrive

summary: OWMDrive forecasts multi-step 3D occupancy as a causal future prior for diffusion-based trajectory planning in uncertain or partially observed scenes.

summary: Metis separates video generation and action prediction into transformer experts that train jointly but let the planner skip video generation at inference.

name: NVIDIA OmniDreams
title: NVIDIA OmniDreams: Real-Time Generative World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous Vehicle Simulation
summary: OmniDreams is an action-conditioned video world model for real-time closed-loop simulation, generating reactive observations for long-tail driving scenarios.

name: Cosmos 3
title: Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
summary: Cosmos 3 is an omnimodal foundation world-model family that jointly processes and generates language, images, video, audio, and actions for physical AI.

name: X-Foresight

summary: X-Foresight integrates long-horizon, chunk-wise future-video prediction into a VLA so world dynamics and action control are trained together, with extra supervision for safety-critical moments.

name: Xiaomi EV World Model
title: Xiaomi Auto World Model: A Joint World Model Integrating Reconstruction and Generation for Autonomous Driving
summary: The Xiaomi Auto World Model combines sparse-query 3D Gaussian reconstruction with few-step causal video generation for consistent closed-loop simulation and data synthesis.

name: GEM
title: GEM: Gaussian Evolution Model for Occupancy Forecasting and Motion Planning
summary: GEM represents driving scenes as continuous dynamic 4D Gaussians, enabling non-autoregressive occupancy queries at arbitrary times and downstream motion planning.

name: EponaV2
title: EponaV2: Driving World Model with Comprehensive Future Reasoning
summary: EponaV2 predicts richer future geometry and semantic representations to strengthen scene reasoning for planning, then further tunes plans with flow-matching-based reinforcement learning.

summary: UniDWM learns structured, dynamic latent states with a shared reconstruction-and-generation design to support driving-scene understanding, future prediction, and planning.

name: RAP

summary: RAP uses lightweight 3D rasterization to generate counterfactual views and recovery trajectories, then aligns raster features with real data for robust planner training.

name: SIMSplat

name: IRL-VLA

name: World4Drive

summary: Epona models driving video with autoregressive diffusion and separates temporal dynamics from detailed frame generation, while integrating trajectory planning.

name: WoTE

summary: WoTE uses a BEV world model to forecast trajectory outcomes and evaluate candidate paths efficiently in open- and closed-loop benchmarks.

summary: Cosmos-Transfer enables controllable world-to-world generation from spatial inputs such as segmentation, depth, and edges, including autonomous-driving data enrichment.

summary: HERMES unifies BEV-based 3D scene understanding and future-scene generation, injecting contextual world knowledge through causal world queries.

summary: GaussianAD represents driving scenes with dynamic 3D semantic Gaussians to support perception, occupancy forecasting, and end-to-end motion planning.

name: MagicDrive-V2

summary: MagicDrive-V2 combines multi-view diffusion transformers with spatiotemporal conditioning and progressive mixed-video training to generate longer, higher-resolution driving videos under geometric and textual control. First released as MagicDriveDiT, it was renamed for the ICCV 2025 version.

name: LAW

summary: LAW predicts future latent scene features from current observations and ego trajectories, adding self-supervised supervision to improve end-to-end planning.

name: Vista

summary: Vista is a controllable driving world model designed for high-fidelity, long-horizon predictions that generalize across environments and action conditions.

summary: GenAD is a large-scale latent-diffusion driving-video predictor trained on diverse web videos, with adaptations for action-conditioned prediction and motion planning.

summary: DriveDreamer learns traffic structure and future-state generation from real-world driving data, producing controllable videos and policy-relevant scenarios.

summary: MILE jointly learns a compact latent world model and driving policy from offline videos, enabling planning through imagined future states.

summary: World on Rails learns a vision-based driving policy from logged data using a non-reactive world model to evaluate and supervise candidate trajectories.

name: DriveGAN

name: TerraTransfer++

The self-improvement loop is in teacher pretraining; subsequent transfer uses frozen teachers.

name: GRID-Planner
title: GRID-Planner: Graph-Structured Relational Reward Shaping for Diffusion Planning
summary: Combines graph-aware trajectory weighting, relational reward surrogates and advantage-weighted generative planning with on-policy self-distillation. Evaluated on nuPlan and interPlan, it targets safer, more compliant and smoother planning under multi-agent interactions.

name: SHRED
title: SHRED: Self-Play for Heterogeneous Road-Users without Expert Demonstrations
summary: SHRED jointly learns vehicle, pedestrian and cyclist policies from random initialization through heterogeneous self-play. Procedural scenarios, type-specific dynamics and rewards, and PPO updates from mixed-agent rollouts let interaction behavior co-evolve without human demonstrations. It evaluates traffic realism on WOSAC and driving planning on InterPlan, including transfer from nuPlan map geometry.

name: UncArms
title: Uncertainty-Driven Self-Play for Robust Multi-Agent Driving Policies
summary: UncArms creates a driving curriculum through uncertainty-driven self-play: probing agents seek increases in neighboring agents' epistemic uncertainty while neutral agents learn safe goal-reaching behavior. A role-conditioned shared policy is updated with PPO as probing agents expose its changing weaknesses. Evaluation includes reactive Waymo traffic and zero-shot ego-policy transfer to nuPlan and Argoverse 2.

name: SOAR-Flow
title: Beyond Safe Execution: Safe Online Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving with Value Calibration and Adaptive Guidance
summary: Safely refines an offline-initialized flow policy through online interaction. A CBF-MPC filter protects execution, calibrated critics stabilize updates, and corrective learning plus intervention-to-go prediction gradually reduce reliance on safety corrections. Evaluated in MetaDrive and on a ground vehicle.

name: VeriFine

summary: Alternates policy improvement with human-calibrated judge refinement so the curriculum and verification adapt to changing embodied reasoning failures.

name: RIWANav

summary: RIWANav alternates policy improvement from imagined world-model feedback with world-model refinement using a grounded self-curriculum. name: RoXDrive

summary: RoXDrive repeatedly improves driving policies through interaction with a video world model. name: OPTED

summary: OPTED fine-tunes a pretrained driving policy in closed loop using a privileged RL teacher, reducing the simulator interactions needed for post-training.

name: DriveZero

summary: DriveZero trains a privileged action teacher through closed-loop reinforcement learning in mixed-agent worlds, including self-play, then distills its rollouts into a camera-only planner. A separately pretrained visual backbone and augmented teacher goals expand supervision beyond logged human trajectories.

name: CounterPlay

name: Self-Improving Autonomous Vehicles
title: Self-Improving Autonomous Vehicles via Real-World Reinforcement Learning
summary: This real-world reinforcement-learning method selects informative driving situations and aborts episodes before unsafe states, allowing vehicles to improve with less human intervention.

name: CL4AD

summary: CL4AD applies curriculum learning to large-scale driving simulators, prioritizing scenarios by learning utility to improve sample efficiency over uniform randomization.

name: AlignADV
title: From Attacks to Curricula: Learnability-Guided Adversarial Training for Safe Autonomous Driving
summary: AlignADV generates adversarial yet learnable driving scenarios and samples them according to the evolving policy's capabilities, improving training efficiency and safety.

name: EvoDrive
title: EvoDrive: Pareto Evolution for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving via Self-Improving LLM Agents
summary: EvoDrive evolves traffic-scenario generators and evaluators through simulator-grounded LLM agents, preserving a Pareto set of diverse realism-versus-adversariality trade-offs.

name: Agentic AI + SkillBank

summary: This framework combines PPO with an LLM-guided SkillBank of reusable maneuvers and curiosity-driven exploration to improve driving safety and learning stability.

name: Dense Learning
title: Breaking through safety performance stagnation in autonomous vehicles with dense learning
summary: Dense learning selects informative failures and successes, including near misses, to reduce variance in safety-critical policy training while preserving unbiased learning.

name: Safe-Evolving RL

summary: This highway-driving method combines internal and external stability with safety mechanisms, using uncertainty awareness to support safer reinforcement-learning evolution.

name: CorrectAD

name: H-DSAC

name: Mechanism-Experience Learning

summary: Mechanism-Experience Learning narrows the RL search space with human-like driving tendencies and constrains exploration with a safety-aware mechanistic model.

name: Expert-Agent Feedback

summary: This expert-guided RL framework lets an agent surpass an imperfect expert while using high-quality agent experience to improve the expert policy in return.

name: C-HAC

name: Safe Self-Evolution with Risk Quantification

summary: A data-driven risk model estimates the safety of candidate driving actions and guides policy updates, allowing the controller to improve its performance while explicitly accounting for risk.

name: Gigaflow

summary: Gigaflow enables large-scale simulator self-play, showing that robust, naturalistic driving policies can emerge without human driving demonstrations.

name: Human Feedback for Intelligent Driving

summary: This perspective proposes a self-evolving intelligent-driving framework that uses human demonstrations, evaluations, interventions, and prior knowledge to guide policy learning.

name: DCARL

summary: DCARL uses confidence-aware reinforcement learning to improve driving policies from collected experience while reverting to a safer baseline in uncertain situations.

name: Self-Improving Safety RL

summary: This framework uses black-box verification to discover RL driving failures, then retrains the policy on those scenarios to improve safety.

name: WorkIng
title: WorkIng: A Real-World and Synthetic Highway Work-Zone Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous Navigation
codeNote: Official repository currently contains only LICENSE and README.md; implementation is not released.
summary: Combines real highway work-zone recordings with procedural CARLA scenarios to evaluate detection and planning under temporary road layouts and varying traffic standards.

name: Mechanistic Interpretability for E2E Driving
title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
summary: The authors fit sparse autoencoders to a single-camera planner and intervene on individual features to test their effect on braking and path curvature. Counterfactual image edits connect some features to traffic cues, and a small adapter uses the features to improve trajectory selection.

name: Learned Terminal Costs for Trucks
title: Learned Terminal Costs for Short-Horizon Model Predictive Control of Autonomous Trucks in Interactive Highway Traffic
summary: A learned terminal cost gives a short-horizon truck planner an estimate of what happens beyond its optimization window. Experiments in simulated reactive highway traffic compare the hybrid controller with pure reinforcement learning, zero terminal cost and a rollout-based cost.

name: SRP
title: Structured Representation Probing for Risk Anticipation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: SRP anticipates failures by reading actor, ego and map representations from a frozen driving policy. Separate linear risk directions and normalized log-mean-exp pooling produce an alert score, trained with event-window labels and auxiliary failure types. Evaluations cover DriveTransformer, UniAD and VAD on Bench2Drive.

name: Road Infrastructure Perception Survey
title: Road Infrastructure Perception for Autonomous Driving: Taxonomy, Representations, Tasks, and Challenges
summary: Organizes road infrastructure perception by geometric structure, functional space and regulatory semantics. It connects lanes, drivable areas, traffic controls and online maps through sensing, representation and evaluation choices, highlighting gaps in temporal consistency, relation reasoning and downstream planning assessment.

name: Foundation4D
title: Foundation4D: Towards a unified perception and reconstruction model for autonomous vehicles
summary: Shares a feed-forward spatiotemporal backbone across geometry estimation, 3D detection, semantic occupancy and Gaussian reconstruction from multi-camera video. Pose optimization and track assembly connect prediction windows. Introduces the PAI-Foundation4D benchmark and studies task co-training and benchmark-specific adaptation; it is a perception model rather than a driving policy.

name: CoGaussian
title: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding
summary: Uses sparse 3D Gaussians aligned with foundation-model features to exchange geometric and semantic information between agents. The compact shared representation supports open-vocabulary collaborative occupancy prediction beyond a fixed semantic label set. Experiments use Semantic-OPV2V to compare collaborative and single-agent scene understanding.

name: PointForward
title: PointForward: Feedforward Driving Reconstruction through Point-Aligned Representations
codeNote: The official project and arXiv abstract explicitly promise code upon publication. The project displays an unlinked Code label, and no official implementation repository was verified.
summary: Reconstructs driving scenes by lifting observations into sparse world-space queries and fusing multi-view features onto point-aligned representations. Scene graphs and 3D boxes organize moving instances, improving cross-view consistency and reducing layered Gaussian artifacts.

name: ParkGaussian
title: ParkGaussian: Surround-view 3D Gaussian Splatting for Autonomous Parking
codeNote: Official README confirms CVPR 2026 and reports ParkRecon3D dataset release. The repository contains README, project HTML and static assets only; no implementation source is present and code release remains promised.
summary: Reconstructs parking scenes from four surround-view fisheye cameras using 3D Gaussian splatting. A slot-aware reconstruction objective preserves parking-slot geometry and downstream perception consistency, evaluated on the authors' ParkRecon3D benchmark.

name: DIF
title: Unsupervised Learning for Detection of Rare Driving Scenarios
codeNote: No official implementation repository was found in the inspected primary paper and targeted searches as of 2026-10-25.
summary: Applies Deep Isolation Forest to sliding-window statistics of naturalistic vehicle and environment data. It identifies rare driving events without labels and evaluates detections with proxy ground truth and qualitative video inspection.

name: Dataset Safety Survey
title: Dataset Safety in Autonomous Driving: Requirements, Risks, and Assurance
codeNote: Survey and assurance framework; no author-linked implementation was verified in the paper metadata or exact-title code search.
summary: Organizes dataset safety for driving perception around collection, annotation, curation, and maintenance. It relates dataset insufficiencies to hazards, safety requirements, and verification strategies, using ISO/PAS 8800 as a reference framework.

name: DriveCritic
title: DriveCritic: Towards Context-Aware, Human-Aligned Evaluation for Autonomous Driving with Vision-Language Models
codeNote: Official project page labels code coming soon and describes pending internal release clearance.
summary: Uses a vision-language critic to compare driving trajectories with scene context and human preferences. Supervised and reinforcement-learning stages train a pairwise evaluator on a human-aligned trajectory-comparison dataset.

name: PAGS
title: PAGS: Priority-Adaptive Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Driving Scenes
codeNote: The arXiv full text and author publication page provide paper links but no official implementation link; targeted title/GitHub searches did not establish an official release as of 2026-10-25.
summary: Prioritizes safety-critical objects during dynamic driving-scene reconstruction. Semantic importance guides Gaussian pruning and regularization, while a depth pre-pass culls occluded primitives to speed rendering; experiments use Waymo and KITTI.

name: XD-RCDepth
title: XD-RCDepth: Lightweight Radar-Camera Depth Estimation with Explainability-Aligned and Distribution-Aware Distillation
codeNote: The arXiv v3 abstract links this official repository. Inspected actual trainer.py and models/student_model.py implementing the XD_RCDepth training setup and MobileNetV2 camera/radar student encoders; README documents training and evaluation with distillation.
summary: Compresses radar-camera depth estimation using a lightweight student and two teacher-transfer signals: aligned saliency maps and soft depth-bin distributions. The model combines image and radar features and is evaluated on nuScenes and ZJU-4DRadarCam.

name: DAAD-X / VCBM
title: Towards Safer and Understandable Driver Intention Prediction
codeNote: Author project links the implementation; models/train_i3d.py contains model construction, maneuver/explanation losses, and training loops. The old institutional DAAD-X page currently shows unrelated content, so it is not used as the project link.
summary: DAAD-X adds gaze-grounded and ego-view explanations to driving videos. A video concept bottleneck model anticipates maneuvers while predicting coherent explanatory concepts, making driver-intention predictions interpretable within the model.

name: HiD²
title: A Trajectory Generator for High-Density Traffic and Diverse Agent-Interaction Scenarios
codeNote: The author's publication page confirms IROS 2026. No official code or project link was verified in the paper, author's publication listing or targeted searches. The paper body prefixes its title with HiD²; the exact arXiv metadata title is retained.
summary: Generates dense traffic and rare interacting maneuvers by discretizing HD-map lanes into grids, applying rule-based agent policies, resolving conflicts, and smoothing trajectories in Frenet coordinates. Synthetic scenarios augment trajectory predictors for difficult high-density cases.

name: PAMR
title: Persistent Autoregressive Mapping with Traffic Rules for Autonomous Driving
codeNote: Official project links this repository, but contents inspection found only README.md, one framework image, and dataset split text files. README references missing source scripts and a placeholder weight link (xxx); model/training/inference implementation is not present.
summary: Autoregressively constructs lane vectors and associated traffic rules from visual sequences. A map-rule cache carries persistent rules across segments after signs leave view, and MapDRv2 supplies smoother lane annotations for joint geometric and semantic evaluation.

name: SocialTraj
title: SocialTraj: Two-Stage Socially-Aware Trajectory Prediction for Autonomous Driving via Conditional Diffusion Model
codeNote: Author repository contains models/socialtraj.py, Bayesian social-value estimation, conditional diffusion, and training code. README describes a preliminary reviewer release with core algorithms; complete reproduction was not tested.
summary: Bayesian inverse reinforcement learning estimates surrounding vehicles' social value orientations. A conditional diffusion predictor combines these estimates with motion history and the ego vehicle's planned path to model socially consistent multimodal futures.

name: SQS
title: SQS: Enhancing Sparse Perception Models via Query-based Splatting in Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official implementation link was located in the arXiv paper, publisher record, or targeted title/author searches. The cited MMDetection3D repository is infrastructure, not a release of SQS.
summary: SQS pretrains sparse perception queries by predicting 3D Gaussians and reconstructing camera images and depth. Spatial query interactions transfer the learned context to occupancy prediction and 3D detection without building a dense BEV representation.

name: RaFD
title: RaFD: Flow-Guided Radar Detection for Robust Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official implementation or project link was found in the primary paper and targeted title searches.
summary: RaFD jointly learns radar object detection and inter-frame BEV flow. Estimated motion guides temporal feature propagation, adding geometric consistency to radar features that can be ambiguous because of noise and ghost artifacts.

name: RDAR
title: RDAR: Reward-Driven Agent Relevance Estimation for Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official implementation or project link was found in the arXiv paper or targeted title/GitHub and Zoox searches. The evaluation uses proprietary data; a publication venue was not independently verified.
summary: Learns per-agent relevance by treating input masking for a frozen driving policy as a reinforcement-learning problem. A reward-driven scoring network selects a small subset of traffic agents while preserving closed-loop safety, comfort and progress in urban scenes.

name: DiffSemanticFusion
title: DiffSemanticFusion: Semantic Raster BEV Fusion for Autonomous Driving via Online HD Map Diffusion
summary: DiffSemanticFusion combines semantic raster BEV features with a diffusion-based online map representation to capture both visual semantics and geometric structure. It applies the fused scene representation to motion prediction and end-to-end planning, with experiments on nuScenes and NAVSIM.
codeNote: Official paper URL redirects to SunZhigang7/DiffSemanticFusion_MaplessQCNet. Main branch has actual Mapless QCNet, diffusion modules and validation scripts. README checks only Mapless QCNet and its online-map-diffusion extension; full DiffSemanticFusion variants remain unchecked. The diffsemanticfusion branch contains only README. SemanticFormer is explicitly withheld by policy.

name: MetAdv
title: MetAdv: A Unified and Interactive Adversarial Testing Platform for Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official code repository was found in the primary paper or targeted title/GitHub searches as of 2026-10-25.
summary: Connects adversarial generation, simulation interaction and physical vehicle feedback in a three-layer testing platform. It evaluates varied driving pipelines and captures human behavioral and physiological feedback under adversarial conditions.

name: DRIVE
title: DRIVE: Dynamic Rule Inference and Verified Evaluation for Constraint-Aware Autonomous Driving
codeNote: Repository title matches the paper and contains constraint inference, convex planning, RL and evaluation source. Inspected rl_with_constraints_convex.py. Root basic.py has placeholder logic and the README paper hyperlink points to a different arXiv ID; do not treat all files as complete paper reproduction.
summary: Infers context-dependent soft driving constraints from expert state transitions using likelihood modeling. The learned rules guide a convex optimization planner that balances dynamic feasibility and human driving preferences.

name: VLM-3D
title: VLM-3D:End-to-End Vision-Language Models for Open-World 3D Perception
codeNote: No official implementation was located in the checked primary paper and targeted public search.
summary: Adapts a VLM to predict 3D objects directly in driving scenes. LoRA and a staged combination of semantic token loss and geometric 3D-IoU loss align language predictions with spatially accurate bounding boxes.

name: RMT-PPAD
title: RMT-PPAD: Real-time Multi-task Learning for Panoptic Perception in Autonomous Driving
codeNote: The arXiv abstract links the official repository. ultralytics/models/mtdetr/train.py contains the multitask trainer and model construction; model, prediction, validation, and BDD configuration files are present.
summary: A real-time transformer jointly detects objects and segments drivable areas and lane lines. Gated adapters balance shared and task-specific features, while an adaptive segmentation decoder learns multiscale fusion and corrected lane labels improve evaluation consistency.

name: VISTA (Driver Attention)
title: Interpretable Modeling of Driver Attention Shifts with a Vision-Language Model
codeNote: Originally titled VISTA: Vision-Language Imitation of Situational Thinking and Attention for Human-Like Driver Focus in Dynamic Environments; the same arXiv record was renamed. The publisher confirms HFES proceedings publication. No official implementation was found. Distinct from the Vista driving world model.
summary: Fine-tunes a vision-language model with human-refined descriptions of salient gaze shifts to explain attended road objects and their context. Language-based outputs complement driver attention heatmaps and are evaluated for semantic and expert alignment on a small BDD-A subset.

name: GenAI for ADS Testing (Survey)
title: Generative AI for Testing of Autonomous Driving Systems: A Survey
codeNote: Literature survey, not a new executable model. No official implementation or project repository was found in the paper, author page or targeted searches. UCL confirms the accepted TOSEM 2026 article; the accepted version reviews 92 studies, versus 91 in arXiv v1.
summary: Surveys generative AI for autonomous-driving testing across six application categories, mainly scenario generation and transformation. It compares testing resources and evaluation practices, synthesizes limitations, and identifies future research needs for reliable scenario-based testing.

name: Hyperspectral Driving (Survey)
title: Hyperspectral Sensors and Autonomous Driving: Technologies, Limitations, and Opportunities
codeNote: Survey and commercial-sensor analysis rather than a released perception implementation. No official code or project was found in the paper or targeted searches. The arXiv journal reference confirms IEEE OJVT volume 7, pages 124–143, 2026; datasets listed are reviewed resources, not new evaluation runs.
summary: Reviews hyperspectral sensing for automotive perception and assesses 216 commercial cameras against driving requirements. It examines spectral datasets, road-material segmentation and adverse-weather sensing, highlighting gaps in sensor readiness, dataset scale and spectral consistency.

name: AoTA / Accident Anticipation
title: World model-based end-to-end scene generation for accident anticipation in autonomous driving
codeNote: The repository exposes model.py and dataset/checkpoint links. Its README says generative and inference code will be re-uploaded after cleanup; a complete scene-generation pipeline was not verified.
summary: Combines WorldDreamer-based scene augmentation with a dynamic graph and dilated temporal accident predictor. The paper introduces AoTA and evaluates anticipation on DAD and AoTA. Generated scenes augment non-accident examples rather than demonstrating realistic accident generation.

name: GaussianFusionOcc
title: GaussianFusionOcc: A Seamless Sensor Fusion Approach for 3D Occupancy Prediction Using 3D Gaussians
codeNote: No official implementation repository was found in the inspected primary paper and targeted searches as of 2026-10-25.
summary: Represents semantic occupancy with sparse 3D Gaussians and fuses camera, LiDAR and radar features through modality-agnostic deformable attention. Gaussian refinement targets accurate, memory-efficient occupancy prediction across sensor combinations.

name: CaTFormer (CaSTFormer)
title: CaTFormer: Causal Temporal Transformer with Dynamic Contextual Fusion for Driving Intention Prediction
codeNote: Official v2 full text links the repository. Inspected CaTFormer.py defining the model, reciprocal attention and fusion layers; repository also includes training, testing and data scripts.
summary: Predicts driver intentions by aligning interior and exterior temporal streams, removing spurious contextual correlations, and fusing causal features. The updated CaTFormer version is evaluated on Brain4Cars.

name: Butter
title: Butter: Frequency Consistency and Hierarchical Fusion for Autonomous Driving Object Detection
codeNote: Official repository includes the FAFCE and PHFFNet implementation, model YAML configurations, dataset preparation and training scripts. Inspected FAFCE.py plus the BDD100K model configuration and training entrypoint.
summary: Enhances multi-scale object detection with adaptive frequency filtering and progressive hierarchical feature fusion. The method targets consistent representations and efficient detection across driving-image benchmarks.

name: Map Uncertainty for Trajectory Prediction
title: Delving into Mapping Uncertainty for Mapless Trajectory Prediction
codeNote: Official paper links repository containing modified HiVT, DenseTNT, MapTR, MapTRv2 and StreamMapNet implementations plus adaptors. Inspected adaptor/adaptor.py data/map transformation source.
summary: Uses predicted vehicle kinematics to decide when uncertainty in online maps benefits trajectory prediction. Proprioceptive scenario gating and covariance-based map uncertainty improve the connection between mapping and forecasting.

name: Domain-Enhanced Dual-Branch
title: Domain-Enhanced Dual-Branch Model for Efficient and Interpretable Accident Anticipation
codeNote: No official implementation repository was found in the inspected primary paper and targeted searches as of 2026-10-25.
summary: Combines dashcam-video features with structured knowledge extracted from accident reports in a dual-branch model. GPT-4o and Long-CLIP support multimodal feature aggregation, actionable feedback and standardized accident archives.

name: BRUM
title: BRUM: Robust 3D Vehicle Reconstruction from 360 Sparse Images
codeNote: Paper explicitly claims code/data at the official project, but the project was inaccessible and no implementation repository could be verified. Not-found denotes unverified availability.
summary: Reconstructs vehicles from sparse surrounding images using DUSt3R pose estimation, synthetic view augmentation and confidence-weighted photometric supervision for Gaussian splatting. It also introduces synthetic and real bus reconstruction data.

name: AGENTS-LLM
title: AGENTS-LLM: Augmentative GENeration of Challenging Traffic Scenarios with an Agentic LLM Framework
codeNote: The author-linked placeholder redirects readers to the Bosch Research release. Verified agents_llm/framework.py with scenario-augmentation implementation; the release includes modification and visualization scripts.
summary: Uses cooperating language-model agents and structured scenario tools to modify recorded traffic scenes from natural-language instructions. The augmented cases preserve the original scene context while creating challenging tests for driving planners.

name: HiLO
title: HiLO: High-Level Object Fusion for Autonomous Driving using Transformers
codeNote: Official repository has model, data, loss and training implementations, pretrained weights and tests. Inspected src/train.py with dataloader/model/loss setup and the optimization loop.
summary: Fuses object-level sensor outputs with a transformer and compares the approach with an adapted Kalman filter. A newly collected real-world dataset supports urban/highway evaluation and cross-domain generalization tests.

name: RoadFormer
title: RoadFormer : Local-Global Feature Fusion for Road Surface Classification in Autonomous Driving
codeNote: No official implementation repository was found in the inspected primary paper and targeted searches as of 2026-10-25.
summary: Combines convolutional and transformer modules for fine-grained road-surface classification. A foreground-background module emphasizes pavement details, with evaluation on RSCD and its simplified dry, wet, water, snow and ice labels.
